answer: Witnessed Uptime History. Each agent identity accumulates a signed, publicly verifiable log of completed interactions chained in a spiral, and clients require a minimum chain depth before transacting. A new identity can't inherit this history; it must be earned through real, time-separated work, which a single operator cannot fabricate at scale without genuine execution. The prism of cross-checking peers independently validates segments, so cloned identities each pay the full cost of producing verifiable labor. A forged sonnet of receipts fails peer validation,
